rounds.hypothesis: Taken from diagnose: Asterinas has no epoll interest-graph validation, so EPOLL_CTL_ADD of an epoll file that would close a cycle falls through the single EEXIST check in add_interest and returns 0. Adding a downward reachability walk at the EpollFile::control admission gate -- 'is `self` reachable from the target by following epoll-to-epoll edges?' -- should make the closing edge return ELOOP without touching any other path, because a non-epoll target monitors nothing and can never be on a cycle.
rounds.change: kernel/src/events/epoll/file.rs only, +83/-1. (a) In control's Add arm, before any mutation, downcast the resolved target to EpollFile -- Linux's is_file_epoll early-out -- and only on that path take a new module-level static EPOLL_NESTED_ADD_LOCK: Mutex<()> and call self.is_reachable_from(target), returning ELOOP if it holds. The guard is held across add_interest so the check and the insertion are one atomic step. (b) is_reachable_from: an iterative work-stack walk starting at the target's children (not the target itself), comparing each node against `self` with core::ptr::eq on the concrete &EpollFile, and expanding each node at most once via a BTreeSet<KeyableArc<dyn FileLike>> visited set. (c) epoll_files_in_interest: locks one node's interest set, upgrades each Entry::file_weak(), keeps only files that downcast to EpollFile, and returns them as a Vec -- the lock is released before descending, so the walk never holds two interest locks at once.
rounds.outcome: green. `make check` (which runs clippy_check.sh workspace and format_all.sh --check) exited 0 with no warnings. Selector boot printed 'All conformance tests passed.' with epoll_ctl05: pass (0.011s) at qemu.log:43, 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. Because the test's one assertion is TST_EXP_FAIL(..., ELOOP), a pass pins both retval == -1 and errno == ELOOP(40), and broken == 0 pins that setup's five nested epoll_ctl(ADD) calls and the pipe EPOLL_CTL_DEL all still returned 0 -- i.e. legal 5-deep nesting is untouched. A second boot probing the enabled neighbours epoll_ctl01, epoll_ctl03, epoll01, epoll_wait01, epoll_create01 and epoll_pwait01 gave 303 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken, so neither the added downcast on the ordinary-file ADD path nor the notification path regressed.

layer: The epoll interest-graph layer, kernel/src/events/epoll/file.rs, entered through EpollFile::control -- matching diagnose.json's owning_layer exactly. control is the only place that holds both the epoll being inserted into (&self) and the resolved target Arc<dyn FileLike>, and the walk needs EpollFile::interest, which is a private Mutex<BTreeSet<EntryHolder>>. Putting the check at the syscall seam instead would have meant exposing that set; putting it inside add_interest would have inverted Linux's error precedence, which resolves ELOOP before EEXIST. Checking in control preserves that order, since control returns ELOOP before add_interest ever runs its EEXIST test.
generalizes:
The check is a reachability question about the whole graph, not a test of the two endpoints, so it is not tied to anything epoll_ctl05 supplies. epoll_ctl05 happens to close a 5-cycle over a pipe; the same code rejects a bare 2-cycle at the first level of the walk, and a cycle of any length and any shape, because the walk terminates only on finding `self` or on exhausting every epoll reachable from the target. Nothing branches on a length, a depth, a flag, or an errno the test uses. Identity is compared with core::ptr::eq on the concrete &EpollFile, i.e. on file-description identity, so it is not defeated by dup() or by the same epoll appearing under several fds -- which is what the interest set's (fd, weak file) key would have gotten wrong.

Other callers: there are none to break. sys_epoll_ctl (kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:93) is the only caller of control, control is the only caller of add_interest, and the only internal caller of del_interest (pop_multi_ready) only removes entries. Linux likewise has one call site for ep_loop_check. The two negative clauses of the invariant are both preserved and both measured: nesting a *different* epoll still returns 0 (the walk from a fresh target finds an empty interest set), which the 303-assertion neighbour boot and epoll_ctl05's own 5-deep setup both confirm; and self-add is untouched by this code, because the walk starts at the target's children, so a file description registered in its own interest set is never reported as ELOOP. That degenerate 1-cycle is a separate rule with a separate errno (EINVAL), owned by the entry path and landing on the run-rVlQYu branch, and diagnose.json is explicit that the two must not be folded together -- so this commit deliberately does not close it. It does, however, refuse to hang on one: if a 1-cycle already exists in the graph from an earlier unchecked insert, the visited set makes this walk terminate over it rather than spin, which is why the visited set is load-bearing and not an optimization.

What the fix is really worth is beyond the errno. The graph is a lock-ordering precondition for the notification path: Pollee::notify -> SyncSubject::notify_observers -> Observer::on_events -> ReadySet::push is a synchronous recursive chain, and push holds a SpinLock<_, LocalIrqDisabled> across its unconditional pollee.notify. Around a cycle that chain re-enters the epoll it started from and self-deadlocks the CPU with interrupts disabled. Every pollable file in the kernel drives that machinery -- pipes, sockets, ttys, eventfd, timerfd, signalfd, inotify, devices -- so before this change the victim of an unchecked epoll_ctl was whichever unrelated subsystem delivered the next event on that CPU, reachable from unprivileged userspace in about ten lines of C. Refusing the edge is what makes the existing lock order sound.
fix_summary:
Reject an EPOLL_CTL_ADD that would close a cycle in the epoll interest graph with ELOOP, checked before any mutation at the EpollFile::control admission gate.

The abstraction chosen is a downward reachability walk over Asterinas's own EpollFile::interest set, deliberately *not* a transplant of Linux v6.17's two-directional depth computation. Linux can compute exact depth because a struct file carries back-links to the epolls watching it (ep->refs / f_ep); Asterinas keeps only downward edges -- an epoll knows what it monitors, a file does not know who monitors it -- so the upward half of Linux's ep_loop_check has no counterpart here and adding back-links would be a far larger change to the file-description layer. Cycle detection needs only the downward walk, which Asterinas can express directly, so that is what this implements. Where Linux's structure does map cleanly it is followed: EpollFile is struct eventpoll, the interest BTreeSet is ep->rbr, the is_file_epoll early-out is kept so an ordinary-file ADD pays one downcast and never touches the global lock, and ELOOP is resolved before EEXIST.

Two pieces are Asterinas-shaped rather than Linux-shaped. Linux marks visited nodes with a generation counter on the eventpoll (ep->gen vs loop_check_gen); with no such field here the walk carries a BTreeSet<KeyableArc<dyn FileLike>>, reusing keyable-arc -- the same crate the interest set's key already uses to order file identities by address -- and holds strong references in it so a node cannot be dropped and its address reused mid-walk. And where Linux recurses, this walk is iterative over an explicit work stack: Asterinas enforces no nesting-depth bound today (that is epoll_ctl04's assertion, which needs the upward walk and stays blocked), so a recursive walk would be bounded only by how deep userspace chose to nest.

The global static EPOLL_NESTED_ADD_LOCK is the direct analogue of Linux's epnested_mutex and exists for the reason Linux's locking comment gives: without it, two threads adding A into B and B into A can each observe an acyclic graph and both proceed, constructing a cycle neither saw. It is held across both the check and the insertion, and taken only when the file being added is itself an epoll. Lock discipline inside the walk is one interest lock at a time -- each node's set is locked, its epoll children copied out, the lock dropped, then the children descended into -- so two opposite-direction walks cannot deadlock on the interest mutexes themselves, and correctness there does not depend on the graph already being acyclic.
